title: Commercial Lease Renewal Newcastle: Build Your Timeline Before the Notice Window
excerpt: Plan backwards from your lease-specific notice dates, then compare renewal, relocation and workplace costs with a clear owner for each decision.
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Renewal Newcastle: Planning Timeline | YOS
metaDescription: A practical Newcastle commercial lease renewal timeline: confirm notice windows, compare costs, plan make-good and align your team before committing.
author: Your Office Space
body:
## When should a Newcastle business start planning a lease renewal?

Start by finding your earliest relevant notice date, rather than counting backwards only from lease expiry. Have your solicitor confirm the option window, notice requirements and any other lease-specific conditions, then allow time before that window to compare staying with realistic alternatives.

The stages below are a business planning framework, not statutory deadlines. Office, industrial and retail premises can have different rules. The NSW retail leasing sources below are useful context, but your solicitor should confirm whether those rules apply to your premises.

## Stage 1: Build a verified dates register

Collect the signed lease, variations, side letters and any earlier renewal documents. Ask your solicitor to confirm the dates and the required method of giving notice. Record an internal decision date earlier than the legal deadline and nominate a backup person.

| Item | What to record | Helpful action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lease expiry | Confirmed expiry date and supporting document | Keep the source document with the register |
| Option window | Opening and closing dates, if an option exists | Ask your solicitor to check the exercise requirements |
| Rent review | Method, timing and outstanding information | Separate confirmed figures from assumptions |
| Exit and make-good | Obligations, access and proposed handback date | Obtain scope advice before budgeting |
| Business approval | Who can decide and who can sign | Allow time for board or finance approval |

[Organise your lease critical dates](/tools/critical-dates)

## Stage 2: Test the workplace before negotiating

Write a one-page brief covering peak attendance, meeting rooms, parking, accessibility, storage and realistic growth. For a Newcastle or Lake Macquarie team, test the daily journey from the places your staff and customers actually travel from. A preferred suburb is a starting point; access and suitability need checking at the individual property.

Helpful tip: ask staff to identify the task the current office makes hardest. Separate a layout or furniture problem from a building limitation before assuming relocation is required.

[Build your space brief](/resources/office-size-calculator)

## Stage 3: Compare renewal with credible alternatives

Put the proposed renewal and suitable alternatives into the same comparison period. Include rent, reviews, applicable outgoings, incentives, fitout, furniture, transition costs and current lease exit obligations. Label every input as confirmed, quoted or estimated.

Ask for the basis of each market comparable: location, size, condition, lease terms and whether the figure is an asking rent or an evidenced agreement. A headline rent from a different building is not a complete comparison.

Helpful tip: keep upfront cash requirements separate from total occupancy cost so an attractive overall option does not hide a difficult moving period.

[Compare commercial lease options](/resources/lease-comparison)

## Stage 4: Decide before your internal deadline

Have the business decision-maker, tenant representative and solicitor work from the same brief. Tenant representation supports the commercial comparison and negotiations; your solicitor advises on legal rights, documents and notices. Confirm who will issue any required notice and how its delivery will be evidenced.

If a deadline is close or may have passed, obtain legal advice promptly rather than assuming discussions with the landlord preserve an option.

Helpful tip: keep a short decision record explaining the preferred option, unresolved conditions and the person responsible for each next step.

## Stage 5: Plan the transition or refresh

A renewal may still require furniture changes or works in an occupied office. A relocation needs a delivery programme covering design, relevant approvals, contractor appointments, IT, furniture, occupation and current premises handback. Confirm actual lead times with the appointed providers.

YOS can coordinate client-side FitOut project management alongside tenant representation and furniture planning. Construction is carried out by appointed contractors.

[Compare renewing with relocating](/blog/renew-or-relocate-commercial-lease)

[Plan the workplace handover](/blog/office-fitout-handover-checklist)

## Frequently asked questions

### Is lease expiry the deadline for exercising an option?

Do not assume so. Check the option window and requirements in your lease with your solicitor. The date for taking action can be earlier than expiry.

### Does every commercial lease have an option to renew?

Check your documents rather than assuming an option exists. Ask your solicitor to explain your position and the steps available if a fresh agreement is needed.

### Can we use a standard twelve-month timeline?

Use a planning checklist as a starting point, then work backwards from your verified dates and actual project needs. A complex relocation may require more preparation than a straightforward renewal.

### Can YOS help with a Newcastle lease renewal?

Yes. YOS can help develop the brief, assess alternatives and negotiate commercial terms alongside your legal adviser. Bring the lease documents, current costs and your team's priorities to the first conversation.
